items.title: AI Unicorn Valuations Soar as Bridgewater Bets Big on Hardware—Cloud Giants Tighten Grip on Compute Power — BigGo Finance
items.snippet: The artificial intelligence industry is witnessing an accelerating concentration...
items.raw_snippet: The artificial intelligence industry is witnessing an accelerating concentration of capital and resources among a handful of dominant players. Anthropic completed a new $30 billion funding round in just three months, sending its valuation skyrocketing from $380 billion to $900 billion and leapfrogging OpenAI to become the world's most valuable AI unicorn, with annualized revenue surging past $45 billion. Driving this shift, Microsoft, Amazon, and Google have effectively seized control of the compute lifelines of nearly all top-tier AI labs through equity investments bundled with long-term cloud contracts, a dynamic that has triggered antitrust investigations by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and the European Union. At the same time, hedge fund titan Bridgewater Associates made sweeping adjustments to its portfolio in the first quarter, placing heavy bets on AI chips and cloud hardware while liquidating traditional software stocks—a clear signal that Wall Street is repricing value across the AI industry chain.

items.title: Rethinking portfolio construction at the human-AI nexus - Top1000funds.com
items.snippet: As artificial intelligence models become more sophisticated, asset owners and ma...
items.raw_snippet: As artificial intelligence models become more sophisticated, asset owners and managers are rethinking portfolio construction as an activity sitting at the nexus of human and machine, which means gaining an edge over the market increasingly needs investors to tap into the wisdom from both sources. At the Top1000funds.com Fiduciary Investors Symposium in Singapore, Temasek head of quantitative strategy and performance analytics Kevin Chang said the $324 billion Singapore-headquartered global investment firm sees a dual role for AI in the investment process: to get better predictive signals and to enhance analytical methodologies. Chang leads the quantitative and systematic strategies team from the Singapore office and said the investor started utilising AI to harness better signals as early as a decade ago. “What ends up happening is that we can often… push the expected returns a little higher, but of course, whatever that is, whether it’s positive or negative in a given month or a given quarter, it’s always going to be small relative to the contribution of the stock pickers in the first place.”.
